guideTitle: The Best Standing Desk Converters Under $100 for a Single-Screen Desk
metaDescription: Around $100, standing desk converters are manual and compact. We compared six on platform width, profile and price, and flag which sat just above $100 when we checked.
introParagraphs: A converter under $100 is a way to try standing without replacing your desk, but the budget sets clear limits. Every converter here is manual rather than electric, and the platforms are 24 to 30 inches wide, which suits one monitor or a laptop plus a keyboard rather than a dual-monitor setup.
Before comparing models, measure two things: your desk's depth, since the converter's base needs room, and your desk's height, since even at its lowest setting a converter raises your keyboard.

Prices move around $100: three VIVO models were listed at $99.99 at the time of writing, while two picks were above $100 and one was well under. Our comparison is based on published specifications and price position, not hands-on testing.

b09vmnymy3-under100.summary: VIVO's 26-inch converter, the most widely purchased here, listed slightly above $100 at the time of writing.
b09vmnymy3-under100.description:
The VIVO DESK-V026KB is the most established converter here, with the largest base of buyer feedback, but it was listed at about $108 at the time of writing, slightly above the budget.

Its 26-inch platform suits a single monitor or laptop.

If it drops under $100 when you shop, it is a sensible default; otherwise, the VIVO 28-inch or 29-inch model is within budget.
cons: Slightly above $100 at the time of writing
b09vmnymy3-under100.bestFor: Readers who can stretch slightly past $100 for the most established model.
b09vmnymy3-under100.skipIf: Your budget is firm; the VIVO 28-inch was listed at $99.99.

b07k8wz19k-under100.description:
The VIVO DESK-V000U gives the widest VIVO platform within budget: a 29-inch single-top surface at $99.99 at the time of writing.

A single top holds the monitor and keyboard on one surface, which is simpler but places the keyboard at the same height as the monitor base.

It sits right at the ceiling with no margin, so a small price change could push it over.
pros: At $99.99 at the time of writing
cons: Few specifications in the listing summary
b07k8wz19k-under100.bestFor: One monitor and a full-size keyboard on a single surface.
b07k8wz19k-under100.skipIf: You want a slimmer profile; the VIVO Ultra-Slim is designed for that.

b0f8114738-under100.summary: A 28-inch VIVO converter at $99.99, with slightly more positive buyer feedback than the 29-inch model.
b0f8114738-under100.description:
The VIVO DESK-V028S is the value pick within a firm $100 budget: a 28-inch platform at $99.99 at the time of writing, with somewhat more positive buyer feedback than the 29-inch VIVO.

It suits a single monitor or laptop.

Like the other VIVO models at $99.99, it sits right at the ceiling.
pros: Within budget at the time of writing
cons: Few specifications in the listing summary
b0f8114738-under100.bestFor: A single-monitor setup within a firm $100 budget.
b0f8114738-under100.skipIf: You need a very low profile; the VIVO Ultra-Slim is thinner.

b08gkxxt22-under100.summary: VIVO's ultra-slim single-top riser at $99.99, designed to add as little height as possible.
b08gkxxt22-under100.description:
The VIVO Ultra-Slim is the pick if you're worried about a converter raising your seated keyboard height: its low-profile design is intended to add as little height as possible when lowered.

It is a compact single-top riser, $99.99 at the time of writing.

The compact platform leaves limited room for more than a laptop or one small monitor and a keyboard.
pros: Within budget at the time of writing
cons: Exact dimensions not in the listing summary
b08gkxxt22-under100.bestFor: Desks already at a comfortable seated height, where every inch of added height matters.
b08gkxxt22-under100.skipIf: You need more surface; the VIVO 29-inch is wider.

b0765bq7rn2-under100.summary: A 30-inch gas-spring converter from Mount-It!, listed well above $100 at the time of writing.
b0765bq7rn2-under100.description:
The Mount-It! converter offers the widest platform here, 30 inches, with a gas-spring lift, but it was listed at about $129 at the time of writing, well above the budget.

Mount-It! specializes in ergonomic mounts and stands.

Consider it only if the extra width matters or it goes on sale below $100.
cons: Well above $100 at the time of writing
Few specifications in the listing summary
b0765bq7rn2-under100.bestFor: Readers who want the extra width and can wait for a sale.
b0765bq7rn2-under100.skipIf: You need to stay under $100; the VIVO 29-inch is close in width.

b0d1c9lbn5-under100.summary: A 24 x 14-inch extra-slim manual converter at about half the price of the VIVOs.
b0d1c9lbn5-under100.description:
The Aconcept Extra-Slim is the lowest-cost way to try standing: a 24 x 14-inch manual converter at about $50 at the time of writing, half the price of the VIVO models.

Its extra-slim design should add little height when lowered.

The small platform fits a laptop more comfortably than a monitor and keyboard, and buyer feedback is less extensive and less positive than for the VIVO options.
cons: Suits a laptop more than a monitor
b0d1c9lbn5-under100.bestFor: Trying a standing setup with a laptop for as little as possible.
b0d1c9lbn5-under100.skipIf: You use a monitor and full keyboard; the VIVO 28-inch gives more room.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A converter adds height even when lowered. Check its lowest platform height against your seated keyboard height; slim designs like the VIVO Ultra-Slim and Aconcept add less.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Match platform width to your setup
buyingCriteria.explanation: Platforms here run from 24 to 30 inches, which suits a laptop or one monitor plus keyboard. Dual monitors generally need a wider converter than this budget allows.
The base can be deeper than the platform. Measure desk depth and check the listing's base dimensions.
Every converter here is manual. Electric converters typically cost more than $100.

faq.a: The VIVO 28-inch (DESK-V028S), listed at $99.99 at the time of writing, with positive buyer feedback.
The Aconcept Extra-Slim, at about $50 at the time of writing.

faq.q: Can a converter under $100 hold two monitors?
faq.a: The platforms here, 24 to 30 inches wide, are better suited to one monitor or a laptop. Dual monitors generally need a wider platform.
No. All the converters here use manual or gas-spring lifts.

faq.q: Will a converter make my desk too high when seated?
faq.a: It can. Check the converter's lowest height; the slim models here are designed to add less.

bottomLine: Within a firm $100 budget, the VIVO 28-inch is the sensible default for one monitor, the 29-inch gives a little more width, and the Ultra-Slim adds the least height to a desk that's already the right seated height.
The Aconcept Extra-Slim halves the cost for a laptop setup. The VIVO 26-inch and Mount-It! were above $100 when we checked, so consider them only if their prices drop.
